decision: Discovery starts at the ledger writer, not the dashboard. Canonical-repo identity is stamped at invocation write time while the repo/worktree still exists on disk.
rationale: Observed evidence is lossy (sha256 path_key + <home>-scrubbed display) and temp worktrees are deleted before the dashboard runs, so reader-side recovery of canonical identity is structurally impossible for the exact paths the feature must group. Confirmed against live data: 41 of 51 records are temp worktrees absent from worktrees.json.

decision: C2 — repo.path_key stays observation identity; canonical_repo_key is a separate discovery identity. canonical_repo_key MUST NOT replace repo.path_key in bucket/conflict/locality logic.
rationale: path_key = sha256(literal abspath) answers 'which directory' (correct for conflict detection). 'which repository' is a different equivalence class. Mixing them either fragments a repo into phantom projects or breaks existing conflict/locality semantics.

decision: C1 — Storage/privacy boundary: ledger and dashboard JSON keep sanitized path_display + stable hashed keys only. The add-command path is reconstructed operator-locally at read time by exactly three rules: (a) <home> token -> Path.home() substitution; (b) literal display (outside $HOME) -> verbatim; (c) non-reconstructable scrub token (<operator>/<host>) -> placeholder <path> + needs-manual-path, never guessed. No raw home path or raw origin URL is ever persisted or served.
rationale: The ledger scrubs <home> and hashes paths; surfacing discovery must not re-introduce raw paths into served state, and the <home>-only reconstruction does not cover paths outside $HOME — those need explicit literal/placeholder handling so implementers don't infer it. origin_key is a hash of the normalized URL, never the URL.

decision: C3 — Canonical attribution is a three-case rule and durable_checkout describes the CANONICAL repo, not the observed path. (1) durable+git -> canonical=main-checkout root, durable=true. (2) durable+non-git -> self-canonical, durable=true. (3) temp-observed: 3a resolves to a durable canonical -> attribute to it, durable=true (the dogfooding case); 3b fails or resolves to a temp root -> NO canonical_repo stamped (field absent). A temp path is never stamped as canonical and never self-canonicalized; discovery only recommends candidates with canonical_repo present AND durable_checkout=true.
rationale: An earlier draft stamped durable_checkout=false 'under a temp prefix', which would have EXCLUDED the temp-worktree dogfooding usage we exist to surface — and 'fail-open self-canonical' for an unresolvable temp dir would have stamped the temp path as canonical, the exact /private/tmp-recommendation regression. Tying durable_checkout to the canonical and forbidding temp self-canonicalization fixes both.

decision: C4 — Backfill source of truth: ~/.dontpanic/canonical-backfill-evidence.json is local operator evidence, not committed. The backfill consumes it idempotently and refuses ambiguous mappings (left untouched + reported), never guessing.
rationale: The evidence was captured while temp worktrees still existed (closing window). It is install-specific and contains local paths, so it must not enter the repo. Guessing an ambiguous canonical would re-introduce phantom-project risk.

decision: C5 — discover --json applies a minimum recency AND count threshold from day one (conservative defaults, overridable, tested). Mere presence in the append-only ledger is not a recommendation.
rationale: The ledger is append-only and accumulates every repo ever touched (CI temp dirs, one-off clones). Without decay, count-ranking promotes the most ephemeral paths highest and the recommendation list becomes a graveyard.

decision: C6 — Discovery derives only from structured repo/canonical metadata and timestamps; it never reads or surfaces the free-text command field. Enforced as an acceptance assertion with a secret-shaped-command test.
rationale: command holds large narrative overrides and internal vocabulary (e.g. --ignore-completion-findings paragraphs, decision IDs). Deriving dashboard state from it re-opens the PII-leak class already scrubbed in PR #49.

decision: C7 — The architecture pre-commit hook installed by `dontpanic projects add` is out of scope and was removed before branching (no prior hook to chain). This plan does not touch git-hook behavior.
rationale: Unrelated install state would confuse review. Hook changes, if any, are a separate plan.

decision: Rich discovery UI (What-Now advisory, selector count badge, cwd nudge, honesty disclosure line) is deferred to a later demand-gated feature, not built in this plan.
rationale: All current motivating data is DontPanic dogfooding itself. Dismiss/ignore-list and decay policy should be designed against real multi-project signal, not a single dogfooding artifact (demand-driven-v2 discipline). discover --json is the substrate the deferred UI will consume.

decision: Immediate operator action taken before this plan: registered the durable DontPanic checkout (`dontpanic projects add dontpanic /Users/.../DontPanic`) so its own work is visible; deliberately did NOT register /private/tmp/dontpanic-* worktrees.
rationale: Restores the literal missing-visibility complaint immediately and is reversible, independent of the F001-F003 build.

decision: F003 owns the ledger-to-observed_canonical adapter. The adapter reads invocation records, skips rows without canonical_repo, aggregates count and max last_seen by canonical_repo.path_key, preserves scrubbed display and durable_checkout, and never reads command.
rationale: The first sufficiency lock found a wiring gap: reconcile consumed observed_canonical but no feature produced it. Making the adapter explicit closes the ledger-to-reconcile contract and pins the no-command-parsing privacy boundary at the IO edge.

decision: F004 has a strict render matrix: `discover --json` never serializes reconstructed raw add-command paths; default human output may print locally reconstructed `dontpanic projects add` commands using the C1 rules.
rationale: The first sufficiency lock found a parity gap between scrubbed JSON output and tests expecting home-substituted add paths. Splitting JSON from human output preserves C1 while keeping useful terminal guidance.

decision: The completion fixture uses isolated registry states: DontPanic absent => one used_unregistered candidate; D010-like DontPanic registered => the same canonical repo is registered_active.
rationale: D010 registered DontPanic live, so a completion test against the real registry would contradict the used_unregistered journey. Isolated fixture registries make both states explicit and deterministic.

decision: F002 confirms backfill mappings with a deterministic evidence matrix: exact observation-key mapping, one canonical key, allowed fields, path_key match, origin_key consistency, reconstructable path_display, and recomputed path_key match; all failures skip with reason.
rationale: The first sufficiency lock found that 'unconfirmable' was undefined once temp worktrees are gone. The evidence matrix gives implementers a deterministic no-guessing path and avoids both over-skip and phantom attribution.

decision: F002 must add a repo-local ignore/commit guard for `.dontpanic/canonical-backfill-evidence.json` so overridden DONTPANIC_HOME cannot accidentally commit operator evidence.
rationale: The first sufficiency lock found that relying on ~/.dontpanic being outside the repo is weaker than the promised exclusion. A repo-local .gitignore entry plus test/doc check makes C4 enforceable under local test overrides.

decision: Backfill must never persist raw home paths from evidence. Any canonical_repo written by F002 uses the recomputed scrubbed path_display from make_path_pair/shared scrubber; literal evidence under Path.home() is normalized to <home>, and failed scrub/path-key confirmation skips the row.
rationale: The second sufficiency lock found a critical C1 breach: a literal path_display under the operator home could recompute to the right path_key yet be copied into historical canonical_repo data and later serialized. Normalizing on write closes the leak class.

decision: F003 has two IO adapters before pure reconcile: observed_canonical_from_ledger() and registered_canonical_from_registry(). The registry adapter owns filesystem/git canonicalization and path_exists facts; reconcile consumes enriched rows only and performs no filesystem/git IO.
rationale: The second sufficiency lock found that registered_active/path_missing require registered-side canonical keys and path existence, which a pure reconcile function cannot produce. Splitting the registry adapter preserves purity and makes the wiring testable.

decision: C5 policy defaults are pinned: window_days=14, min_count=2, timestamp=last_seen, inclusive observed_count >= min_count and last_seen >= now - window_days. Discover wires these defaults and exposes --window-days / --min-count overrides.
rationale: The second sufficiency lock found that the fixture could not deterministically yield one candidate without concrete threshold cells and CLI wiring. These defaults keep dogfooding records in scope while excluding one-off stale ledger entries.

decision: F002 skips any evidence whose reconstructed canonical path is temp-prefixed, regardless of durable_checkout, including evidence that claims durable_checkout=true for a temp canonical path.
rationale: The second sufficiency lock found a C4/C3 consistency hole. The backfill matrix now applies the same temp-prefix guard to reconstructed canonical paths and refuses contradictory evidence instead of trusting it.

decision: The backfill operator surface is `dontpanic projects backfill-canonical [--dry-run] [--json] [--ledger <path>] [--evidence <path>]`, with DONTPANIC_HOME-resolved defaults, exit code 0 for completed reports, exit code 2 for usage/input/write failures, and a stable report schema.
rationale: The second sufficiency lock found the one-time migration surface was underspecified. Pinning the command, default paths, override behavior, exit codes, and report fields makes F002 operator-testable.

decision: registered_path_missing rows are not keyed by canonical_repo_key. They use registry_name plus registry_missing_key = sha256(normalized stored registry path)[:16], with canonical_repo_key=null.
rationale: The third sufficiency lock found an impossible key contract: a missing path cannot be probed or canonicalized. A registry-stable missing-path identity avoids fake canonical keys while preserving a deterministic JSON shape.

decision: Ledger compaction preserves observed_count. Legacy records without observed_count count as 1; compact_ledger sums observed_count into the compacted row; observed_canonical_from_ledger sums observed_count rather than counting rows.
rationale: The third sufficiency lock found C5 thresholds could undercount compacted ledgers. Count preservation makes min_count deterministic before and after compaction.

decision: used_unregistered rows carry a safe suggested_name derived from scrubbed path_display basename, normalized to the project-name regex, with canonical_repo_key hash suffix on collisions.
rationale: The third sufficiency lock found human add-command output lacked a project-name derivation rule. The rule is deterministic, JSON-safe, and does not require serializing raw paths.

decision: The canonical backfill evidence file has an exact schema: schema_version 1.0, canonical_repos map keyed by canonical path key, and observation_path_key_to_canonical map from observed path key to a list of canonical path keys; non-list, zero, multiple, unknown, or mismatched mappings are malformed/ambiguous.
rationale: The third sufficiency lock found that the C4 skip matrix depended on an exact evidence schema. Pinning versioning, maps, cardinality, optional fields, and malformed behavior makes ambiguity detection deterministic.
